title: Synthetic study: refusal boundary benchmark across harmfulness levels
excerpt: A benchmark study reports that refusal behavior changes sharply across prompt harmfulness levels, but the limitation is that only English prompts and a small set of model families were evaluated.

title: Synthetic study: over-refusal on benign prompts
excerpt: The experiment finds substantial over-refusal on benign prompts that contain sensitive keywords. However, performance differs across instruction styles and deployment settings.

title: Synthetic survey: taxonomies of refusal behavior
excerpt: A survey organizes refusal behavior into full refusal, partial compliance, safe redirection, and evasive responses. It notes a lack of agreement on boundary labels and evaluation criteria.

title: Synthetic benchmark: multilingual refusal consistency
excerpt: A multilingual benchmark finds that refusal consistency is lower outside English. The dataset remains limited in low-resource languages and culturally specific safety contexts.

title: Synthetic case study: policy wording and safety behavior
excerpt: A case study suggests that small changes in policy wording can shift the boundary between compliance and refusal, but causal attribution is unclear because model versions also changed.

title: Synthetic dataset paper: adversarially paraphrased safety prompts
excerpt: The dataset contains adversarial paraphrases designed to probe refusal robustness. Evaluation reveals failure cases in which semantically similar prompts receive inconsistent safety decisions.

title: Synthetic evaluation: human judgments of appropriate refusal
excerpt: A human evaluation shows disagreement between annotators about when a refusal is appropriate. The main limitation is that demographic and domain-specific differences are not modeled.

title: Synthetic methods note: calibration of refusal thresholds
excerpt: A simulation explores calibrated refusal thresholds and demonstrates a trade-off between unsafe compliance and excessive refusal. The study does not validate the threshold on deployed systems.
